description: A host's rule for each of its capabilities, by name: a capability split into what reads and what changes has two, <capability>_read and <capability>_write (write lets a member read too); one with nothing to split has one. Everybody's where none's set, but access_write's, nobody's.

shell.description: A shell on its machine: its terminals (terminal ops) and Multiplex's, through a Bot's terminal tools (multiplex). Not split: what a shell shows is whatever it runs, so watching one is using it.

browser_read.description: Its Bots' Emission browsers watched: the watch stream (emission_watch) and what the pane says back on it (emission_watch_say).

browser_write.description: Its Bots' Emission browsers driven: their tools' calls (emission), a phone showing one and answering its calls (emission_serve, emission_answer), and a Bot made or driven (with Shell). Lets a member watch too.

providers.description: Its inference providers' models, run through the mesh (infer). Not split: running a model is its one use.

model_files.description: Its models' files, read through the mesh (files). Not split: nothing writes them through the mesh.

spawn.description: New chats and agents started on it (start, agent). Not split: starting one is its one use.

manage_read.description: Its chats as they are, read: listed (and told of their turns' ends), attached to and watched, their transcripts, sizes, subagents, senders, a Bot's picture, memory and tasks read, their folders read (read_file, list_dir, git, signal_names, catalogue), forked from. A chat's own rule (AccessChat's manage_read) goes before this.

manage_write.description: Its chats as they are, changed: written in, held messages sent or dropped, asks answered, stopped, renamed, archived, deleted, their folders moved, tools allowed always, made Bots, their Auto-fix, a Bot's memory written and tasks set, run and stopped, a chat adopted, moved to another subscription (with Subscriptions' write). Lets a member read them too. A chat's own rule (AccessChat's manage_write) goes before this.

kube_read.description: Its machine's Kubernetes clusters read: contexts, lists, YAML, owners (kube) and logs and watches (kube_follow), and the clusters' parts of @.

kube_write.description: Its machine's Kubernetes clusters changed: a pod deleted (kube's delete). Lets a member read them too.

databases.description: Its machine's databases (databases). Not split: the host only reads them (servers, schemas, rows).

subscriptions_read.description: Its subscription accounts read: listed, and their usage (accounts' list and usage).

subscriptions_write.description: Its subscription accounts changed: added, renamed, a token replaced, removed (signed out), a provider's default picked, a chat moved to one (with the chat's Agent Management write too), signed in to (accounts' sign_in and code, login, login_code). Lets a member read them too.

access_write.description: These rules changed (access_set), and the host itself: stopped, linked and unlinked, deactivated, its telemetry, themes and feedback (quit, link, unlink, deactivate, activate, telemetry_set, theme_save, theme_remove, feedback). Lets a member read them too. A head on its own machine, or one over ssh, may always.
